purpose: Model-judged audit (three judges plus TypeSafe tiebreak) of the contract v3 gold-gap rule. The column stays a diagnostic beside the v2 headline until this audit passes.
no_document_text: Entries carry document IDs and byte offsets only. Render values and context locally with `gold_gap_evidence.py sheet`.

selection.allocation: every rule-class candidate first (census), then one draw per non-empty sub-stratum and the label floors, then the rest proportional to learned-class label population (largest remainder)
selection.within_stratum: rule-class census first; then labels sorted, per label the ambiguous sub-stratum then the plain one; random.Random(seed).sample over members sorted by (document_id, byte_start)

ambiguity_basis.english_wordlist_rule: lowercase-only entries; the value lowercased is one of them
ambiguity_basis.lowercase_use_rule: a capitalised value whose lowercase form is a letters-only whitespace token outside gold somewhere in the holdout text
ambiguity_basis.unlabelled_use_elsewhere_rule: a capitalised value that occurs on word boundaries outside gold in another holdout document where that value is never gold (German nouns are always capitalised, so Essen the meal never shows up lowercase)

acceptance.rule: at most 4 of 200 answered 'no' or 'uncertain' (uncertain after second adjudication counts as no)
acceptance.bound: Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95 % upper bound on the candidate-level false-credit rate must be at most 5 %
acceptance.clustering: report failures per document as well; if document clustering widens the bound past 5 %, the audit fails
acceptance.design_note: ambiguous shapes are oversampled, so the unweighted failure count is conservative for the population rate; the weighted and byte-weighted rates are reported with the design weights

adjudication.method: Three model judges (Claude Opus drafted first; Codex and TypeSafe judged afterwards, their files sealed by SHA-256 before reading the Opus proposals). 188 cards unanimous. The 12 contested cards were settled by a rule fixed before any re-ask: where TypeSafe sided with a 2-of-3 majority, the majority stands; where TypeSafe was the lone dissent, one fresh TypeSafe Score call (jev-latest, levels no / uncertain / yes, the other two judges' reasons as context) decides at confidence >= 0.8, otherwise the Opus + Codex majority stands. The user confirmed 10 consensus cards by hand; every confirmation matched.
adjudication.delegation: User 2026-09-27, asked how to finish the 12 unclicked contested cards: "Weren't you supposed to use typesafe ai".
adjudication.blinding_limitation: The Codex judge's brief disclosed the Opus aggregate counts and its four no/uncertain card IDs, not the reasons, before judging. TypeSafe saw only the rubric and the card contexts.
adjudication.document_text: Judge reasons, proposals and tiebreak prompts quote synthetic Dataiku document text, so they stay out of this public repo: they are archived in the private CertaMesh/business repo under audits/benchmark/v3-gold-gap-2026-09-27/. This file carries verdict labels, rules and tiebreak probabilities only; `gold_gap_evidence.py accept` checks them against the tiebreak results file.
adjudication.trace_note: The trace this sample was drawn from (sha256 e715a7e9...) is no longer on disk, so the draw cannot be regenerated today. All 200 entries were re-verified against the pinned Dataiku parquet (sha256 916c6379...): the attributed span is gold with the entry's label, the candidate's trimmed bytes equal the gold value, and the candidate overlaps no gold.
